text: Blessed be God, my mountain, who trains me to fight fair and well.
the castle in which I live, my rescuing knight, The high crag where I run for dear life, while he lays my enemies low.
why do you bother with us at all?
we're like shadows in a campfire.
ignite volcanoes in the hearts of the mountains.
shoot your arrows this way and that.
pull me out of the ocean of hate, out of the grip of those barbarians
who shake your hand then knife you in the back.
let me play it on a twelve-string guitar—
the God who rescued David, his servant.
release me from the grip of those barbarians Who lie through their teeth, who shake your hand then knife you in the back.
like sturdy oak trees, Our daughters as shapely and bright as fields of wildflowers.
fill our fields with huge flocks;
eliminate the crime in our streets.
How blessed the people who have God for God!
